subject: MAP + onboarding cadence for evaluation materials (acceptance gates & usage limits)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + onboarding cadence for evaluation materials (acceptance gates & usage limits)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, we can provision the evaluation kit (test cases + prompt pack + a small curated dataset) into a sandbox BrightCart environment. To make sure we close the pilot on a predictable timeline, I put together a short mutual action plan draft attached (MAP-draft-BrightCart-v1.2.pdf) and a manifest of the sample files (eval-kit-manifest.csv).

High-level proposal:
- Week 0 (this week): Share MAP and manifest; procurement to confirm licensing terms.
- Week 1: BrightCart ingests eval kit into sandbox; Redwood provides onboarding call and quick-run acceptance checklist.
- Week 2: BrightCart runs 5 acceptance prompts / regression checks. If acceptance gates pass, move to 14-day expanded pilot.
- Post-pilot: TBD (license/commit) — we can include a short takedown and retention clause in the MAP.

Important usage constraints we need confirmed from your side (so we can finalize the MAP):
1) Allowed recipients for the kit (team members / contractors).
2) Retention window in sandbox (we propose ephemeral 30 days).
3) Logging and audit access (we can provide limited token-level telemetry for the evaluation).

I've attached a small readme for the prompt pack and a CSV manifest. If Procurement is ready, we can add their contract contact to the thread and target a signed MAP by 4/28 to keep the schedule tight.

Next steps: please confirm the procurement contact and any special restrictions (PII, country restrictions) and we will update the MAP.

Best,
Jordan
---
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the clear plan. Procurement (copied) will own the MAP signature, and Sam will be the technical lead ingesting the kit. Quick answers to your questions:
- Allowed recipients: core ML team + 2 external contractors (we'll confirm names once procurement clears NDAs).
- Retention: BrightCart prefers 60 days in a sandbox, but we can accept a 30-day ephemeral lane if Redwood requires it for security.
- PII: The seed dataset contains synthetic PII; procurement will still require a short attestation.

We want to clarify acceptance gates: what does "5 acceptance prompts / regression checks" look like practically? Can you propose a small canonical checklist we can run on Day 7? Also, can we get a short script to automate the runs (just to reduce manual drift)?

Elena
Head of ML Partnerships, BrightCart
[elena.ruiz@brightcart.com]

Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + onboarding cadence for evaluation materials (acceptance gates & usage limits)

Elena —

Welcome on the thread. A couple of practical remarks from sales/procurement side:
1) The MAP we attach typically includes a 30-day ephemeral sandbox by default, but we can toggle to 60 days if you need it. That will affect the limited-use license clause; I'll have procurement draft that variation.
2) For NDAs/contracting speed: if Procurement can sign a one-page MPA (mutual pilot agreement) rather than full enterprise terms, we can start ingestion earlier. I've attached a redlineable MPA template we often use — happy to turn it around quickly.
3) Pricing for the expanded 14-day pilot (post-acceptance) will be shown as a capped pilot fee; I can insert a not-to-exceed number once we agree on the dataset size.

Jordan — can you paste the acceptance checklist and the small automation script you mentioned? Karthik, Marissa: please review the proposed telemetry and retention values (Elena noted synthetic PII).

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + onboarding cadence for evaluation materials (acceptance gates & usage limits)

Quick security notes:
- Synthetic PII is fine from a data-residency perspective but we still need an attestation from BrightCart that the data is synthetic. That can be a single-sentence statement inside the MAP.
- We propose the default telemetry for the assessment: token-level latency/bytes, per-route error rates, and a hashed request-id for traceability. No raw payload retention on Redwood logs unless explicitly requested and signed off.
- Retention: 30 days ephemeral is easier operationally; if BrightCart insists on 60 days we need a signed exception and a follow-up takedown schedule in the MAP (e.g., 60 days then automated deletion + verification report).

Jordan — I'll draft the MAP clause for telemetry + takedown and share a version you can attach to the MPA.

Karthik
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP + onboarding cadence for evaluation materials (acceptance gates & usage limits)

Hi all —

I've attached a concise acceptance checklist and a tiny automation script (prompt-runner.sh) that runs the five canonical prompts and captures per-prompt pass/fail results. The checklist is deliberately lightweight so BrightCart can run it on Day 7 without a lot of manual setup. Summary below:

Acceptance checklist (Day 7):
- 5 canonical prompts executed (script attached).
- For each prompt: top-3 responses compared to expected oracle (fuzzy match threshold 0.78).
- No unresolved PII leakage flag raised (scans included).
- Average inference latency under 350ms for the canonical prompt set.
- Runbook for takedown executed and verified by both parties.

Attachments included: promptpack-sample-README.txt, prompt-runner.sh, acceptance-checklist-day7.md.

If BrightCart is good with this, Jordan/Ben — can we aim to ship the updated MAP (with Karthik's telemetry language) and the redlineable MPA to Procurement by 4/24 so Sam can begin ingestion 4/27? That timeline keeps the pilot close by the end of May and gives both teams time to validate.

Thanks,
Marissa
Product Manager, Eval & E2E, Redwood Inference
